A CrowdStrike update caused global Windows BSODs and boot loops, taking down businesses, banks, airlines, hospitals and 911 services worldwide.
An application shouldn't be able to do this kind of damage to an operating system... maybe it's a Windows bug, more-so than it is a Crowdstrike bug.
'F8 + last known good configuration' worked for us to recover from the boot loop.
I find it amazing that you can have such a functional Ubuntu environment by translating system calls... Microsoft calls it their 'Windows Subsystem for Linux'.
Windows 10 is not bad at all, and I would have enjoyed keeping a Windows 10 machine handy with the new Ubuntu user land support.

They have not removed it, it just is not visible by default if you are connected to the internet. Either run the setup without being connected to the internet, or type in a fake phone number a few times and it will give you the prompt to create a local account.
The online account is crap... I cannot even set a password, it asks me to set up a PIN number to log in.

Before Nadella, Windows wasn't nearly as user-hostile as it is now. There was no mandatory telemetry, there were no forced updates... now they are taking away the ability to use Windows without Microsoft Account.
There is a long-standing Windows bug where local user directory names are created using a truncated version of the online account's name. This is rarely what you want.
I tried with Windows 10, and Windows Server 2019. Windows 2019 is super fast to set up and literally compiled the same c code in half the time it took in Windows 10.
Tracking and privacy on Windows is becoming atrocious, I didn't know about the built-in keylogger until I ran a declutter tool.
Windows 11 also introduced a new sidebar feature with customisable widgets but there was no way to turn off these crappy articles completely.
I always thought Windows did a lot of stuff well (when it was good at least). The telemetry, changing things for the sake of changing things and forced crap constantly being added is enough.
In couple of years Windows 10 will get eol'd and stop receiving security updates... I expect to see additional influx of new Linux users from the eventual eol.
